claims.statement: The main orchestrator for model list generation is in scripts/generate_models.py, containing the generate() function, resolve_profile() helper, PROFILES dictionary, and SCHEMA_VERSION constant.
The is_free() function in scripts/filters.py determines if a model is free by checking if both prompt and completion pricing are "0".

The filter_candidates() function in scripts/filters.py applies thresholds including min_param_b (hard floor), buffered context/output thresholds, require_structured_output, and allowlist/hardallowlist logic.
The PARAM_RE constant and parse_param_count() function in scripts/filters.py extract parameter counts from model IDs using regex.
The fetch_endpoint_stats() function in scripts/endpoint_stats.py retrieves OpenRouter's aggregated endpoint stats for models.
The probe_model() function in scripts/probe.py sends a minimal completion request to test model availability, returning success and latency.
The record_probe() function in scripts/probe.py appends probe results to history files maintaining a 30-day rolling window.
The read_history() function in scripts/probe.py reads probe history from JSONL files for a given model.
The compute_uptime() function in scripts/scoring.py calculates uptime-based scores with NEUTRAL_UPTIME as the default for insufficient samples.
The compute_score() function in scripts/scoring.py combines uptime, latency, and capability scores with configurable weights and latency caps.
The passes_post_probe_filters() function in scripts/scoring.py applies post-probe filters based on OpenRouter's endpoint stats.
The load_thresholds() function in scripts/thresholds.py loads YAML threshold configurations with default fallbacks.
The fetch_models() function in scripts/openrouter_client.py retrieves the OpenRouter model catalog via API.
The mengram thresholds file sets min_param_b: 28, min_context_length: 40000, min_max_output_tokens: 8000, require_structured_output: true, and allowlist: [openrouter/owl-alpha].

The yt-summarizer thresholds file sets min_param_b: 14, min_context_length: 32000, min_max_output_tokens: 2000, require_structured_output: false, and allowlist: [meta-llama/llama-4-scout:free, openrouter/owl-alpha, qwen/qwen3-32b:free].

The openwiki thresholds file sets min_param_b: 70, min_context_length: 128000, min_max_output_tokens: 16000, buffer_pct: 5, require_structured_output: false, require_tools: true, min_candidate_pool: 2, and a seven-model allowlist (thinkingmachines/inkling:free, poolside/laguna-s-2.1:free, cohere/north-mini-code:free, nvidia/nemotron-3.5-lightning:free, google/gemma-4-31b-it:free, google/gemma-4-26b-a4b-it:free, nvidia/nemotron-3.5-super-vl:free) for models without parseable size parameters.
The PROFILES dictionary in scripts/generate_models.py maps profile names to their thresholds and output paths.

The models-mengram.json, models-yt-summarizer.json, and models-openwiki.json files share a schema including generated_at, schema_version, and models array with id, score, context_length, max_output_tokens, uptime, latency_ms, own_uptime, and sanity_ok fields.
The anthropic-models.json file is generated by scripts/generate_anthropic_models.py and contains a sorted array of Anthropic model objects with id, display_name, type, and created_at fields.
History files in the history/ directory store probe results as JSONL objects with timestamp, success, and latency_ms fields, trimmed to a 30-day window.
The update-models.yml workflow runs daily at 03:00 UTC to generate model lists for all three profiles via uv sync and generate_models.py.
The update-anthropic-models.yml workflow runs daily at 03:15 UTC to generate anthropic-models.json via uv sync and generate_anthropic_models.py.
The openwiki-update.yaml workflow runs bi-weekly (gated by ISO week parity) at 05:00 UTC on Saturdays to update OpenWiki using candidate models from models-openwiki.json.
All model list workflows use the concurrency group 'update-model-lists' with cancel-in-progress set to false.

The workflows authenticate using GITHUB_TOKEN for GitHub operations and rely on specific API keys (OPENROUTER_API_KEY, ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, LANGSMITH_API_KEY) stored as secrets for external service access.

The Python environment is managed via uv sync from pyproject.toml on Ubuntu-latest with requires-python >=3.12,<3.15, while Node.js environment uses actions/setup-node@v7 with Node 26 for OpenWiki workflows.
Unit tests cover filter functions (parse_param_count, is_free, supports_structured_output, supports_tools, filter_candidates) in tests/test_filters.py.
Unit tests cover endpoint stats fetching (success, no free endpoints, HTTP error, missing p50) in tests/test_endpoint_stats.py.
Unit tests cover probe functions (probe_model, record_probe, read_history) in tests/test_probe.py.
Unit tests cover scoring functions (compute_uptime, compute_latency_p50, passes_post_probe_filters, compute_score) in tests/test_scoring.py.
Unit tests cover threshold loading (defaults, override, missing keys) in tests/test_thresholds.py.
Unit tests cover OpenRouter client fetching (success, HTTP error) in tests/test_openrouter_client.py.
Integration tests cover the generate() function with mocked dependencies, profile resolution, output schema, probe history, and warnings in tests/test_generate_models.py.

The anthropic-price-aliases.yaml file supplies an aliases map consumed by generate_anthropic_models.py's load_aliases() and join_prices(), letting pricing-page rows be joined to API model ids by slug or by alias when direct slug matching fails.

The history/anthropic-models.jsonl file appends one JSON object per Anthropic model-list run with fields {timestamp, models[]}, preserving run history alongside the committed anthropic-models.json output.

The Anthropic model-list generator (scripts/generate_anthropic_models.py) fetches paginated models from https://api.anthropic.com/v1/models, scrapes the pricing page at https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/about-claude/pricing, joins prices onto model ids by slug/alias, and fails closed (non-zero exit, no output write) on any missing or invalid price to preserve the last-known-good committed file.

The generate_models.py pipeline runs end-to-end as: load thresholds via load_thresholds() → fetch OpenRouter catalog via fetch_models() → filter free candidates via filter_candidates() (hard min_param_b floor, buffered context/output floors, allowlist/hardallowlist bypass, buffer_pct relaxation toward min_candidate_pool) → per-candidate endpoint stats via fetch_endpoint_stats() (NEUTRAL_UPTIME fallback) → probe via probe_model() → record_probe() to history/<model>.jsonl (30-day rolling trim) → read_history() → compute_uptime() → passes_post_probe_filters() → compute_score() (0.6 uptime / 0.3 latency / 0.1 capability, multiplied by own_uptime) → write {generated_at, schema_version: 2, models[]} sorted by score descending.
